subject: Redwood vs Hyperscale: perf follow-up & prioritized lab tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Park <elena@clearsky.health>, Nate Ellis <nate.ellis@clearsky.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscale: perf follow-up & prioritized lab tests

Hi Elena / Nate —

Thanks again for the productive demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you validate internally.

Recap (high level)
- You ran a few UI-driven chats and observed p95 ~280ms and an occasional p99 spike near ~650ms on the hyperscaler endpoint; tokens/sec looks fine for single-tenant flows but degrades under concurrent users.
- Biggest product asks: predictable p95/p99 tail for 2k-token sessions, and stable tokens/sec at 100+ concurrent users (chat workload).
- Procurement asked for a short A/B that compares: Redwood hosted (nvlink+int8) vs HyperscalerX managed endpoint on the same model family.

What we propose
1) Priority test A — P95/P99 tail under interactive chat
   - 2k token sequences, 95% of sessions at target latency <= 350ms, p99 target <= 800ms (initial).
2) Priority test B — Concurrency ramp (tokens/sec)
   - Ramp from 10 -> 200 concurrent chat sessions; measure tokens/sec and queue buildup.
3) Cold-start & cache warm-up check
   - Start with empty KV cache and run 50 synthetic sessions to measure first-token and steady-state deltas.
4) Quantization variant check
   - Run one A/B with fp16 baseline vs int8 quantized model (we'll present quality delta).

Requirements from ClearSky (ask)
- Two representative sample chats (JSON payloads) for the 2k-token test and one short-chat set for concurrency run.
- A service account token or S3 read access to the sample corpus (see related_links).

Owner & timeline
- Redwood lab owners: Marissa (ops lead) + Jonas (bench engineer).
- Proposed lab window: Jun 29 — Jul 3 (we can compress to 48 hours if you prefer).

Attachments: redwood-proposed-test-matrix.xlsx (baseline configs + pass/fail criteria)

Next steps
- Elena/Nate: share the two sample chat payloads and confirm access method (S3 or direct upload).
- Redwood: confirm lab slot and share a read-only results dashboard + RAT (rough acceptance criteria) after tests complete.

If that plan looks good I’ll lock the slot and have Marissa send calendar invites and the lab runbook.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0189
[Attachment: redwood-proposed-test-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Elena Park <elena@clearsky.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Nate Ellis <nate.ellis@clearsky.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscale: perf follow-up & prioritized lab tests

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications before we hand over samples: 

1) p99 tail: procurement cares more about the 99.9th percentile for our clinical UI; if possible include p99.9 as a separate column in results.
2) Concurrency: our expected load pattern is bursty (clinicians logging in at shift change). The 10->200 ramp is fine; can you simulate bursts (e.g., 0->150 in 30s)?
3) Models: we use an open-weights model (same family you have listed in the matrix). We do want to see an int8 quantized run — but keep one run with the exact model we currently use unquantized for quality comparison.

I've attached a small sample set (redacted) and our baseline CSV from last month’s run. The payloads include long context threads to better replicate the tokens/sec behavior.

Files attached: clearsky-chat-traces-202806.zip, baseline-results.csv

We can grant S3 read access — I will loop in Nate to confirm the bucket & credentials. Also, please include a simple cost estimate for each test (rough $/hour) so procurement can evaluate tradeoffs.

Elena
Director of Product, ClearSky Health
elena@clearsky.health
[Attachment: clearsky-chat-traces-202806.zip (zip)]
[Attachment: baseline-results.csv (csv)]

Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscale: perf follow-up & prioritized lab tests

Thanks Elena — got the artifacts.

Quick internal plan:
- Lab slot confirmed: Jun 29 09:00 - Jun 30 18:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).
- Test runner: we’ll run A/B concurrently where possible to minimize variance; Hyperscaler baseline will be exercised from our runner to match traffic profile.
- Configs we’ll run (high level):
   * A: fp16 baseline (Redwood hosted)
   * B: int8 quantized (Redwood hosted)
   * C: HyperscalerX managed endpoint (same model family, vendor config)
- Metrics collected: first-token latency, per-token latency distribution, p50/p95/p99/p99.9, tokens/sec, queue length, and GPU utilization.

Requests for ClearSky:
- Please create an IAM role / service account that grants S3 read to s3://clearsky-samples/chat-samples/jun24/ or provide a secure upload link.
- Let us know any redlines for tests running on vendor infra (e.g., NO_PII policy) — we will scrub what’s required.

Costs: rough estimate is in the attached runbook; we’ll provide a short cost table before the run.

I’m sending the invite now and attaching a small calendar stub. If the team wants a condensed 48-hour window rather than the full slot, flag it and we’ll compress runs.

Marissa Cole

Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscale: perf follow-up & prioritized lab tests

Quick technical notes / clarifications:

- We will capture both cold-start (empty KV cache) and warm-start profiles. Cold-starts typically add ~30-120ms depending on model shard layout; we’ll report both numbers.
- For the concurrency bursts, we will run three burst patterns:
   1) Smooth ramp 10->200 over 10m
   2) Fast burst 0->150 in 30s (matches Elena’s ask)
   3) Sustained high concurrency 120 for 20m to see steady-state queuing.
- Our A/B runner will pin the same sequence ordering across runs to reduce variance from prompt composition.
- We will expose p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + raw per-request logs for opaque inspection (no PII expected in sample files).

If you want an additional check, we can add a tokens/sec throttling test where we artificially cap throughput to observe latency backpressure. Good to do if procurement cares about graceful degradation.

Jonas Weber
Bench Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference
